issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaks into runtime install_requires, not just CI.
issues.detail: The cap belongs in CI scripts where pkg_resources removal actually breaks the mmcv build. Pinning it in core/setup.py's hyperopt extras propagates a CI-only workaround into every downstream install of autogluon.core[ray], constraining users' environments for a transitive build-time issue they will never hit. The invariant 'this pin protects mmcv builds' does not hold at install time of core.

issues.description: mmcv install with --no-build-isolation has unstated build-environment invariant.
issues.detail: Using --no-build-isolation means mmcv's setup.py runs against whatever setuptools, wheel, torch, and numpy already live in the env. The script pins setuptools but states no invariant about torch/numpy/cython presence at this point. If the surrounding CI image changes, this silently breaks. Document the required pre-state (torch installed, setuptools<82, wheel present) in a comment above the call.

issues.description: mmengine pinned to a released wheel without recording why 0.10.7 was chosen.
issues.detail: The prior code pinned a specific git SHA with the comment 'fix for torch 2.5.' The replacement jumps to 0.10.7 with no note on whether that wheel contains the torch-2.5 fix the SHA was added for. A one-line comment ('0.10.7 includes the torch 2.5 compatibility fix from <SHA>') would let the next reader verify the regression risk without git-archaeology.

issues.description: mmdet bumped 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0 alongside the build fix, mixing two changes.
issues.detail: This PR is titled 'fix mmengine failure,' but it also moves mmdet a minor version. Two changes, one diff, one rollback unit. If mmdet 3.3.0 introduces a regression, the CI fix and the version bump revert together. A literate commit separates the forced bump (if 3.2.0 is incompatible with mmengine 0.10.7) from the optional bump, or at minimum names the reason in the comment.

issues.description: FIXME comments point at an upstream issue but state no kill condition.
issues.detail: Both FIXMEs reference open-mmlab/mmcv#3325 'remove cap once fixed.' Good. Neither states what 'fixed' looks like in observable terms (mmcv release version, mmengine release, setuptools API restoration). Without a stated revert criterion, this pin will outlive its cause. Add: 'revert when mmcv >= X.Y or when mmengine ships a release that no longer imports pkg_resources at build time.'

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The PR correctly diagnoses the pkg_resources/setuptools>=82 break and caps setuptools in the CI scripts where mmcv builds. The mechanism is sound, but the literate apparatus is thin: the setuptools<82 pin leaks from a CI build constraint into core/setup.py's runtime install_requires, the FIXMEs lack stated revert criteria, and the mmengine and mmdet version bumps arrive without notes explaining why those exact versions preserve prior fixes. Move the runtime pin out of core, document the invariants on the --no-build-isolation install, and name the kill conditions on each FIXME.
